teaches: An explainer: open on what the thing actually is; each part follows from the last (because, therefore, but); the forecast is left out; land on the mechanism's most concrete consequence.

packet.title: How the federal funds rate works
sentences: The federal funds rate is the rate banks charge each other to borrow overnight.
The Federal Reserve sets a target for that rate rather than lending to the public.
Banks build the rates on credit cards, car loans and business loans on top of it.
Mortgage rates track longer-term borrowing costs, which tend to rise with it.
The Fed raises rates when prices are rising too fast.
Higher borrowing costs mean fewer purchases on credit and less business investment, which cools spending.

packet.title: What a rate rise means for savers
sentences: Savings accounts, money market funds and Treasury bonds pay more when rates rise.
A slower economy usually means slower hiring.
Rate changes take months, often more than a year, to reach prices and jobs.

packet.title: Markets look ahead
sentences: Economists expect the Fed to change course next year.
The Fed's chair spoke at a conference in Washington.
